semantic.justification: Original LibreOffice Calendar_gregorian temporal service state and ICU interaction. Root Gregorian construction, system timezone, pending signed16 fields, offset remainders, era mapping and validation follow the pinned source. Display/native-number formatting is a separate unconsumed responsibility. Unconsumed APIs, native ABI/mutex/allocator and undefined-input behavior, complete UNO/display formatting, formatter/column auto-input and final CSV integration remain outside the evidence for this module. No alternate calendar selection or unsupported-known-type error is introduced. Unchanged extracted LibreOffice temporal method bodies linked against unchanged ICU78.3 match2226 field/era/offset/validation cases across seven temporal providers and six zones. Minimal UNO declarations and integral-millisecond RTL round binding isolate this witness; full UNO service registration/display/fractional rounding are not claimed. B8TCAE adds portable replay of2226 independently compiled unchanged original temporal-service observations for7 actual Gregorian/era/Hijri/Jewish service classes,6 timezones, signed dates, pending field order, offsets and invalid normalized dates. Public APIs supply all state; validity, both time forms and all17 source fields are native expectations. The witness uses minimal UNO scalar declarations and an integral-millisecond round binding with original ICU78.3 archives; full UNO ABI, locale-data registration, fractional rounding and display remain unverified. Existing semantic status is unchanged. B8TCAE adds real CalendarWrapper/CalendarImpl integration over registered providers and pinned locale resources: pre-load UNO defaults, UTC forwarding, invalid field indices, failed-ID rollback, locale reload on the same calendar/timezone cache key, independent grammatical name owners, Hanja success and hanja_yoil resource rejection. Source en_US calendar order includes Gregorian and Jewish. Three200000-unit Locale field cases reproduced a JavaScript argument-spread RangeError; LocaleData field lookup now reuses the existing counted-UTF16 text bridge, preserving every input unit and existing direct/language/en_US fallback. No input cap, resource mutation, service replacement or full native UNO-wrapper ABI claim is introduced. Both convenience service loads and actual FormatElement Sequence ownership are checked; a copied General string retains its real sole logical reference after Sequence destruction. Coverage policy and semantic statuses remain unchanged.
